headline: TRUMP-BACKED CRITICAL MINERALS DEALS UNDER FIRE AFTER BLUE WAVE — USA RARE EARTH DROPS 9.5%
snippet: Companies backed by billions of dollars in Trump administration support — including USA Rare Earth, Vulcan Elements, and Kaz Resources — are facing heightened scrutiny after Democrats swept the November 4 midterms and took control of both houses of Congress, per Bloomberg reporting picked up widely on November 8. Democrats now hold subpoena power over the administration's mineral deals, and Senator Elizabeth Warren and other lawmakers had already raised conflict-of-interest concerns about Trump family ties at Kaz Resources (which counts Trump Jr. and Eric Trump among passive investors) before the election. USA Rare Earth fell 9.5% on the news, extending its decline from a 52-week low hit in October; analysts note that executive action on tariffs, stockpiles, and government equity stakes cannot be undone by Congress without beating a presidential veto — but oversight and investigation risk has materially changed the investment thesis for companies reliant on Trump-era policy support.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT TRUCE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 WITH NO RENEWAL IN SIGHT — BINARY CATALYST IN 48 HOURS
snippet: China's suspension of the tougher October 2025 rare earth export controls — most critically the extraterritorial licensing rule that catches foreign-made products using Chinese-origin rare earths above a 0.1% value threshold, affecting chipmakers, defence contractors and industrial manufacturers worldwide — expires on November 10, two days from now, with no renewal announcement from Beijing as of November 8. If China allows the truce to expire, the extraterritorial rule resumes immediately and would force global supply chain certification across defence and technology sectors; if extended, Western rare earth producers lose a near-term pricing catalyst they had been anticipating since October. Pure-play heavy rare earth producers including USA Rare Earth and Energy Fuels' White Mesa separation operations would benefit most from resumption; MP Materials, which mines only light rare earths at Mountain Pass, would see a more modest and indirect pricing benefit.

headline: AUSTRALIA MINERS RAIL AGAINST CGT REFORM — MCA AND AMEC DEMAND EXPLORER EXEMPTION BEFORE 2027 CUTOFF
snippet: The Minerals Council of Australia (MCA) and the Association of Mining and Exploration Companies (AMEC) are intensifying pressure on the federal government this week to exempt mineral explorers from proposed capital gains tax reforms before they take effect on July 1, 2027. The May 2026 federal budget proposal would replace the longstanding 50% CGT discount with cost-base indexation and a 30% minimum tax on gains — a change the MCA models would reduce an individual investor's after-tax return on a small exploration investment by approximately 20%, with the government's proposed carve-out for 'innovative businesses' failing to cover junior mineral explorers. For ASX and TSX-V investors with Australian domicile, the reform threatens one of the core risk-reward incentives that has historically attracted retail capital to speculative exploration equities — the industry's core argument is that Australia cannot accelerate its critical mineral development ambitions while simultaneously reducing the financial incentive for early-stage exploration risk.

headline: U.S. DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY COMMITS $2 BILLION TO CRITICAL MINERALS NATIONAL STOCKPILE
snippet: The U.S. Defense Logistics Agency announced November 6 that it has committed $2 billion from the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act to acquire strategic and critical materials for the National Defense Stockpile, describing the purchases as 'targeted demand signals' designed to help domestic producers start or expand production. Secondary reporting from DLA's Contracting Services Office identifies rare earths, tungsten, titanium, vanadium pentoxide, antimony, high-purity aluminum, and germanium among the targeted materials, though DLA did not publish a full list publicly. For TSX-V and ASX critical mineral developers, the commitment is the strongest U.S. government demand-side signal since the Congressional Critical Minerals Council framework, reinforcing the thesis that government procurement is now a de facto demand floor for strategic minerals — a structural support independent of commodity price cycles.

headline: GOLD GAINS 4.8% FOR THE WEEK TO $4,073 AS AI TECH SELLOFF DRIVES SAFE-HAVEN DEMAND — SILVER UP 5.3%
snippet: Gold rose 4.8% for the week ended November 6 to close at $4,073/oz and silver gained 5.3% to $52.41/oz as a broad technology stock selloff — driven by AI-spending fears and macro de-risking post-midterms — pushed capital into precious metals while crude and copper fell sharply. The simultaneous weakness in AI-linked equities and copper (historically correlated to growth expectations) alongside gold and silver strength reinforces the view that the post-midterm safe-haven trade is structural rather than simply a one-day fiscal fear spike. For junior gold and silver equities, the week's performance adds evidence to the case that the valuation gap between $4,000+ gold and producer multiples is narrowing — though Friday's stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report tested the trade, keeping gold below $4,100 and preventing a decisive technical breakout heading into Barrick's Q3 earnings Monday.

headline: Q2 METALS WINS QUEBEC DISCOVERY OF THE YEAR — CISCO LITHIUM DEPOSIT 295MT @ 1.36% Li₂O RECOGNIZED BY QMEA
snippet: Q2 Metals (TSX-V: QTWO) won the Discovery of the Year award at the 2026 Quebec Mineral Exploration Association Recognition Gala on November 5 for its Cisco Lithium Project — a 41,253-hectare Labrador Trough property with an inferred resource of 295 million tonnes grading 1.36% Li₂O, the deposit remaining open along strike and five drill rigs currently on site. The QMEA award recognizes discoveries that have had a substantial impact on exploration activity in the surrounding region, and Cisco's scale has revitalized lithium exploration across the broader Labrador Trough corridor. For retail investors following lithium juniors in the current oversupply environment, the QMEA award is an independent industry validator that high-quality assets are being recognized regardless of commodity cycle pressure — the distinction between tier-1 lithium discoveries like Cisco and marginal-grade projects is likely to widen as market conditions force capital selectivity.

headline: CRITICAL METALS TAKES 8% STAKE IN BRAZIL'S POWER MINERALS — ADDS SOUTH AMERICAN RARE EARTHS BEFORE NOVEMBER 10 DEADLINE
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. agreed November 7 to invest approximately €3.12 million for an 8% stake in Power Minerals Ltd., adding Brazilian rare earth exploration to a portfolio already anchored by European-linked critical mineral assets. Power Minerals holds rare earth exploration properties in Brazil — a country that ranks among the top global rare earth resource jurisdictions but remains underexplored relative to Australia and China, partly due to historic infrastructure constraints. The deal reflects a broader industry trend of rare earth companies assembling geographically diversified portfolios ahead of the November 10 China export control deadline, with Brazil's combination of proven resource geology, neutrality in U.S.-China trade tensions, and improving infrastructure making it an increasingly attractive jurisdiction for rare earth capital deployment.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT FACES DECEMBER FED HAWKISH RISK — $52 FLOOR HOLDS FOR NOW
snippet: Analysts writing in November 2026 are tracking the tension between silver's projected sixth consecutive annual supply deficit — estimated at 46–67 million ounces by Metals Focus and the Silver Institute — and the hawkish December Federal Reserve path under Chair Kevin Warsh, where the fed funds rate near 4.1% keeps opportunity cost elevated for non-yielding assets. The core paradox: a structural deficit has coexisted with a 29% decline from silver's January record near $121/oz because rising real yields and dollar strength have suppressed institutional investment flows that are the marginal price setter for the metal. For TSX-V and ASX silver explorers, the near-term $50–55 range appears to be establishing a floor supported by industrial demand — but the upside case requires either a Fed pivot or new institutional buying inflows, and neither is confirmed as of the November Silver Institute interim review.

headline: COPPER STALLS BELOW $6.50 RESISTANCE AS AI SPENDING FEARS PERSIST — PHYSICAL YANGSHAN PREMIUM SIGNALS REAL TIGHTNESS
snippet: LME copper is testing the key $6.50 resistance level as the week of November 9 opens, with the DailyForex weekly technical outlook flagging $6.50 as the barrier a sustained rally requires and $6.00 as the floor the bulls must defend — the range reflecting the AI technology sector spending fears that have been the primary driver of copper's paper market weakness since October. The critical divergence: the Yangshan copper premium reached a record $217.50/tonne last week — the highest measure of Chinese physical demand on record — even as LME futures fell to a three-month low, suggesting the paper market is mispricing physical tightness. For TSX-V and ASX copper juniors, the physical signal deserves more analytical weight than the futures chart; the Yangshan premium has historically been a leading indicator of LME price direction, and a record level sustained at current prices suggests a re-rating is building regardless of near-term macro sentiment.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER OUTLOOK: CAN POST-MIDTERM REBOUND SURVIVE BARRICK EARNINGS, THE FED AND IRAN RISK?
snippet: Commodity analysts are framing the week of November 9 as the first genuine test of whether gold's post-midterm rebound — which lifted gold from $3,900 to $4,073 and silver from $48.90 to $52.41 in a single week — can hold above key support levels against three simultaneous headwinds: the December FOMC path under a hawkish Warsh Fed, Q3 earnings from Barrick (November 9), Kinross and Alamos where margin disappointments could trigger sector-wide selling, and ongoing Middle East tension risk that creates competing safe-haven flows into oil over gold. The bull case requires Barrick to deliver margins above 61% EBITDA and either a Fed dovish signal or renewed Iran escalation; the bear case is a Friday jobs-beat replay where gold stalls below $4,100 and miner equities underperform the metal. Investors in TSX-V gold juniors are specifically watching the GDX-to-gold ratio for outperformance — historically the signal that institutional capital is rotating from physical exposure to equity leverage on the gold price.

headline: MIDTERMS RESET U.S. MINE PERMITTING REFORM — WHAT A DEMOCRATIC CONGRESS MEANS FOR JUNIOR MINING TIMELINES
snippet: The Oregon Group's post-midterm analysis argues that the Democratic sweep doesn't simply create oversight risk for Trump-era mineral deals — it also reshapes the landscape for mine permitting reform, an issue where bipartisan support had been building under the FAST-41 framework and pending hardrock mining legislation. With Democrats holding both houses, permitting reform is now more likely to come with strengthened environmental review requirements and longer timelines rather than the streamlined permitting processes miners had been lobbying for — a development that could materially widen the gap between TSX-V-listed greenfield discoveries and eventual production milestones for projects in the United States. The piece identifies one offsetting factor: a Democratic Congress is more likely to protect and expand Inflation Reduction Act domestic production credits and DOE loan guarantees, which benefit advanced-stage critical mineral developers on both sides of the border regardless of which party controls permitting policy.
